clue.text: Armadillo, for example, has plate all round

indicators.note: turned all round, so the word for plate is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer, as of metal or bone

explanation.surface: A natural-history note: the armadillo is the creature that carries armour plating round its body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' turns LAMINA back to front. The armadillo's plates make 'plate' feel like part of the description, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is one example of a beast or creature of the mammal kind.

clue.text: Eternal theme of the beautician?

definitions.meaning: never growing old, lasting for ever
a beautician's sales pitch is keeping clients looking young, free of signs of years

explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never shows years, so the word fits both eternity and the beauty parlour's promise of youth.

clue.text: State aid distributed by the Home Office

indicators.note: handed out in a new arrangement, so the letters of aid are shuffled

parts.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK ministry for policing and immigration

explanation.surface: A government department hands out funding to a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges AID into IDA. The Home Office is the UK government department for policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Leave a musical group — no making a comeback

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: coming back means the word no is read from its end, giving its letters backwards

explanation.surface: Someone quits a band whose career will never revive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone or something is to desert or forsake it, a verb synonym of leave.

clue.text: Hesitated to have father taken advantage of

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
used means exploited, taken advantage of

explanation.surface: Someone wavers at the thought of their dad being exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs in the past tense describe stopping briefly before acting, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Beg for a retrial?

definitions.meaning: a legal application to a higher court to have a case heard again

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means plead earnestly; as a legal noun it is the request for a case to be reviewed.

clue.text: Flattery works with EastEnders, say

parts.note: soap is slang for flattery, as in soft soap
opera is the plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that flattery goes down well alongside a TV serial.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British television serial set in London's East End. OPERA, the plural of 'opus', means works.
explanation.definitionFit: EastEnders is an example of a long-running domestic TV drama serial.

clue.text: Refuse to go through all the cases

definitions.meaning: to turn down an offer politely

definitions.text: to go through all the cases
definitions.meaning: in grammar, inflecting a noun through nominative, accusative, genitive and so on

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both turn down politely and, in Latin grammar, list a noun in each of its case forms.

clue.text: Housing allowance

definitions.meaning: lodging, a place to live or stay
making room for something, an adjustment or concession

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lodging and a willingness to adapt or make concessions to others.

clue.text: In truth, she goes to the city

indicators.note: the woman's name goes in front of the city, so removing the city from the truth word leaves her

parts.note: veracity means truthfulness
the word city as written

explanation.surface: A woman truthfully sets off for town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards from the answer: the girl's name plus CITY gives VERACITY, truth, so take CITY away to find her.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a girl's name, so it stands for a woman, she.

clue.text: The acquisition of a favourable reputation

definitions.text: The acquisition of a favourable reputation

parts.words: The acquisition of a favourable reputation
parts.note: being received favourably, gaining approval and a good standing among others

explanation.definitionFit: Gaining approval or a good reception from others is being received favourably, so the phrase describes general approval.

clue.text: Not the first time

definitions.meaning: a sixtieth of a minute, a unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the ordinal after first and a short unit of time.

clue.text: One who talks one round to composing some music

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A speaker brings another person round to the idea of writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Space explorer's study?

parts.note: an astronaut's subject would be the science of stars and planets, not a room in the house

explanation.walkthrough: 'study' suggests a room; it is a field of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of celestial bodies is what someone exploring outer space would naturally study.

clue.text: Restore control, say

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A demand to bring back control, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a mere 'for example' but gives STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone back into a former post or condition is a synonym of restore.

clue.text: Dole out food, say?

indicators.note: signals that the word for food is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute portions, a synonym of dole out.

clue.text: Small child to go out of control

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little child is about to run wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that slides without grip has lost control, as when the tyres lose traction.

clue.text: Lax hands act sycophantically on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the ship one goes on board
to crawl is to fawn or toady

explanation.surface: Idle crewmen suck up to the officers aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means inside SS, the steamship. 'hands' look like sailors but mean handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless, untidy handwriting is a scribble; hands here means styles of writing.

clue.text: Yet it might be the product of an active imagination

definitions.text: Yet it might be the product of an active imagination

parts.words: Yet it might be the product of an active imagination
parts.note: the paradox is that a lazy daydream comes from a busy mind

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical daydream or passing notion, an unproductive thought, which ironically needs a lively mind to produce.

clue.text: Photographed out of doors?

definitions.meaning: of film, subjected to light when a picture is taken
left in the open, without shelter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means film that has had light let in, and also unprotected or in the open air.

clue.text: Smoked by the great man in bed

definitions.note: the definition names something smoked, a noun in sense

indicators.note: the great man is placed in the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a hero is a great man

explanation.surface: A great figure puffs away while lying in bed, like Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, a thing that is smoked.

clue.text: Figurehead at unusually close quarters to the crew

parts.note: the head of the word figure is its first letter, F

indicators.note: done in an unusual way, so the letters of close are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's carved figurehead sits unusually near the sailors' living space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges CLOSE into OCSLE. A figurehead is carved at a ship's bow, the same end as the forecastle.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle, spelt this way in sailors' shortening, is the forward part of a ship where sailors live.

clue.text: Blue-pencil our costs — being out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are jumbled, so the letters of our costs are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor or auditor is told to strike out an improper expense claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to edit by deleting, as with an editor's blue pencil striking text.

clue.text: First of plants underdeveloped, cut back

indicators.note: the first letter of plants is taken

parts.note: read as two words, under developed: the letters of under, developed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener trims back the first of the stunted plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underdeveloped' splits into 'under' and 'developed', which rearranges UNDER into RUNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruned means trimmed or lopped, as a gardener does to shrubs, the same as cut back.

clue.text: Relation who takes the pledge

definitions.meaning: a family member, a parent's brother
slang for a pawnbroker, who accepts pledged goods for a loan

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the pledge' suggests swearing off drink; here a pledge is an item pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a family relative and also old British slang for a pawnbroker.

clue.text: Turkish baths, which flout union regulations?

definitions.meaning: workplaces with low pay, long hours and poor conditions

explanation.definitionFit: Literally places for sweating, like steam baths; usually factories exploiting workers outside trade-union protections.

clue.text: Shut up firm having little work

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A company with not much on goes out of business.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop up is to confine in a small space, like hens in a pen.

clue.text: Journalist taken aback by news of the country

indicators.note: the journalist is taken inside the other word
backwards, so the word news is read from its end

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is startled by news from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reads as startled, but 'aback' turns the news round and 'taken' says the journalist is held within it; 'by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, so it fits as the country named.

clue.text: Notice gap coming in the church calendar

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
a vent is an opening or gap

explanation.surface: A notice about a gap in the church diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent, from Latin for arrival, is the season before Christmas marking Christ's coming.
